mathematical_scope: Phase12 audit constructs a complete binary tree Cayley root-to-leaf column, numeric unitarity/condition/cut statistics for a sampled mixer, and modular inverse/involution checks on sampled vectors. The tree recurrence D[k+2]=D[k+1]+8D[k] and numerator 2·2^depth are specific to coupling alpha=2.
input_and_guard_coverage: Public tree_exact_root_leaf accepts alpha yet expected formula always assumes alpha=2; other alpha values produce a mismatched comparator. No nonnegative integer depth guard. numerical(n) relies on mixer domain; if required_rank is 0 then singular[target-1] indexes the last singular value, not a meaningful threshold. exact_modular accepts trials=0/negative and returns success count 0 without a check. Seeded checks are finite.
cost_and_scaling: Dense S needs O(N²) storage; Gram, condition number and SVD need dense cubic work. Root tree has 2^(depth+1)-1 vertices, exponential in depth. Modular vector checks scale as trials times apply/inverse cost of the unreviewed mixer.
test_evidence: Phase12 test suite uses default alpha=2 for depths1..9, exact trials=4 at N16..256, and separate dense matrix controls. Numeric run covers two cuts at N32,64,128. Numerical values returned by audit.numerical are not asserted there; it only reports passed flags for cuts.
dependency_identity: unitary_mixer exact candidate aff6a16c8c94a6e8db93afbaad9b20d0c20d633c946f1587f51a11df8a7f9ae6 is identity/hash verified only here. NumPy unpinned. Dependency body is not counted as full read.

findings.finding: alpha parameter is forwarded to TreeCayley, but expected recurrence/numerator ignore alpha. The advertised exact formula comparison is valid only at the default alpha=2.
Numerical audit emits errors, conditioning and cut booleans without enforcing global pass criteria; successful execution alone does not mean the stage passed them.
Zero/negative trial counts yield vacuous round-trip reports.

acceptance_boundary: Accept as finite numerical/modular controls at tested default parameters, conditional on exact dependency identity. No all-cut or unbounded-size conclusion.
